artifacts.summary: Empirically re-verified every claimed defect (schema absence, two-vocabulary divergence, stale template/self-healing doc, command-structure.md's 8 defect sites, permissive generate-todo.sh catch-all), found revising/revised to be dead (not just under-documented) vocabulary, confirmed the stale template and self-healing doc are actively injected into live agent context via index-entries.json load_when, and confirmed the validate-state.sh convention should follow the existing hand-rolled bash+jq idiom rather than a JSON-Schema-library dependency.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase has an explicit, documented policy against runtime JSON-Schema-library validators (ajv, python3 -m jsonschema): context/formats/errors-format.md states 'Nothing in core/scripts/ uses one.' All schema validators (events-append.sh, errors-append.sh, validate-handoff.sh) hand-validate via bash case statements, jq-shape checks, and regex checks that mirror the schema file, referenced only in comments. Any new validate-*.sh script should follow this same idiom, not introduce a new external validator dependency.

scripts/lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh is a working precedent for a 'single-source shared library + self-discovering consumer list' pattern in this codebase: it documents its own consumer-discovery mechanism inline ('the current consumer list is found live via grep -rl <libname> agent-system/extensions') instead of maintaining a static consumer list that can drift. This shape generalizes well to any future single-source-of-truth consolidation (e.g. a status-vocabulary.sh shared library).

index-entries.json's load_when wiring (agents/commands/task_types) means a stale or dead-looking context file is not automatically harmless: it can still be actively injected into live agent context. Before treating a doc as 'safe to delete because nothing calls it', check index-entries.json for a load_when entry pointing at it -- a file with zero script/skill callers can still be loaded into every invocation of a specific command or agent via the context-discovery mechanism.
